title: Setting, candidate table, Lean structure, and open math for the A≥3 binding extension
html:
Setting — the A \ge 3 binding gap

The binding-endomorphism analogy closes the deuteron via B = m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \cdot \Delta\mathrm{tr} to +0.19 %, but undershoots A \ge 3 by 44–72 %. Diagnosis: \Delta\mathrm{tr} is the linear truncation of \log(\mathrm{tr}) \sim \mathrm{Vol}; the extensive observable lives in the per-rep q-Reeb rotation phase on the column-rich irrep of a substrate-fixed force-carrier torus knot.

The α_shift universal chain proves \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T_{p, k}) = k \cdot (p - 1) — the pole order of σ on the column-rich irrep, equivalently the boundary holonomy of the Yekutieli non-abelian Stokes integral around the column cycle. This is the same boundary holonomy that the per-rep q-Reeb rotation phase records.

The unification

Per nucleus A, identify the substrate-specific force-carrier torus knot T(p_A, k_A) whose α_shift sets the per-rep Reeb eigenvalue. The binding closure is then

  B(A) = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T(p_A, k_A))
       = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot k_A \cdot (p_A - 1).
nucleus A hypothesised T(p, k) α_shift status
deuteron (D) 2 T(2, 3) candidate 3 open
tritium (T) 3 T(2, 5) candidate 5 open
^3He 3 T(2, 5) candidate (mirror) 5 open
^4He 4 T(3, 4) candidate 8 open

The candidate (p, k) values are hypothesised; the rigorous identification from the substrate's Hecke-Wedderburn block structure on H_{3A}(q) is open.

The deuteron candidate T(2, 3) is motivated by the following rationale:

  1. Smallest non-trivial torus knot. T(2, 3) is the trefoil — the minimum-pole-order column-rich irrep, matching the deuteron's role as the lightest A \ge 2 nucleus.
  2. \mathcal{B}_3-braid-closure consistency. The binding-endomorphism analogy closes the deuteron via B = m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \cdot \Delta\mathrm{tr} to +0.19\,\%. T(2, 3) is the canonical boundary torus knot of \mathcal{B}_3 (the trefoil is the (2, 3)-cable of the core circle in \mathcal{B}_3's Seifert fibre structure).
  3. Calibration consistency. The deuteron's full Markov-weighted q-Reeb phase aggregation gives \rho_{\mathrm{full}}(D) = 14.6673 MeV/rad. With \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 3 and m_e \approx 0.511 MeV, the abstract substrate coupling \rho_0 of the binding factorisation reads \rho_0 = B(D) / (m_e \cdot 3) \approx 1.451 — a dimensionless ratio (its \mathrm{rad}^{-1} unit arises only when the result is re-multiplied by the 14.6673 MeV/rad phase-scale measurement to recover B(D)). Note that \rho_0 (the substrate coupling) and \rho_{\mathrm{full}}(D) (the measured aggregation) are distinct quantities — one is the substrate-universal coupling, the other the per-deuteron phase-weighted aggregation — bridged by the \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 3 normalisation.

This is the A\ge3 analogue of:

  • meson-color-tube-uniqueness for m_K / m_\pi (smallest non-trivial pair \{T(2, 3), T(2, 4)\});
  • the T(2, k) tower for lepton + electroweak masses (W k=4, Z k=6, τ k=7, H k=8).

Structure of the statement

  • Hypothesis 1 (per-rep Reeb phase factorisation). B(A) = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot \alpha_{\text{shift}}(A), where \alpha_{\text{shift}}(A) \in \mathbb{N} is the per-A pole order.
  • Hypothesis 2 (force-carrier knot). The per-A pole order \alpha_{\text{shift}}(A) is realised by the proved formula k(A) \cdot (p(A) - 1) at a substrate-identified torus knot.
  • Uniqueness (conditional on both hypotheses). Two binding evaluators sharing (m_e, \rho_0, \alpha_{\text{shift}}) agree pointwise.

Light-nuclei candidate assignment

The candidate table above is a single assignment covering the light nuclei A \in \{2, 3, 4\}: D \mapsto T(2, 3), T / {}^{3}\mathrm{He} \mapsto T(2, 5), {}^{4}\mathrm{He} \mapsto T(3, 4). With \alpha_{\text{shift}}(A) = k(A) \cdot (p(A) - 1) it gives \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 3 (deuteron), \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 5 (A=3 mirror) and \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 8 (^4He), and it satisfies Hypothesis 2 by construction. The identification pattern is stated once for all light nuclei; identifying (p_A, k_A) from first principles is the open question below.

Remaining open math

What is open is to identify the specific (p_A, k_A) for each light nucleus A. The candidate hypotheses in the table above are informed by:

  • the deuteron's \rho_0 \approx 14.7 MeV/rad calibration from the formal derivation;
  • the mirror pair (T/^3He) \rho \approx 18.5 MeV/rad — ~25 % rise from the deuteron, suggesting a per-λ jump in pole order;
  • the q-Hamiltonian rotational-scale canonical evaluation (the formal derivation) confirms \mu_0 \approx 1.63 MeV is derived from the universal-ilp construction, narrowing the open question to the per-A force-carrier knot choice, not the scale.

Closing it — proving why specifically T(2, 5) carries A=3 mirror binding etc. — requires the per-nucleus minimisation argument on H_{3A}(q)'s Wedderburn block at the binding's smallest non-trivial irrep. The target is a theorem deriving (p_A, k_A) from a Hecke- trace minimisation principle, analogous to the still-open meson force-carrier derivation in Meson m_K/m_π ratio uniqueness via the α_shift universal chain.
